summary: Warm grapes, toasted pita and ricotta salata: pita squares browned in olive oil, halved grapes warmed 30 seconds, tossed with lemon, a spice mixture (fresh zaatar, dukkah, ras el hanout or fennel and cumin), salty ricotta salata and parsley; 10 minutes.
glance: toasted fennel and cumin, zaatar, "fresh zaatar", dukkah or ras el hanout (2-4 teaspoons)
faq: What is ricotta salata?

A variation on fresh ricotta that has been pressed and salted, great for grating or shaving to finish a dish. It is quite salty, so don't eat big chunks, and go easy on adding other salt. Feta would also work well here.
Is this a salad, an appetizer or a side dish?

The author isn't sure either. It combines sweet and salty, crunchy and juicy, herbaceous and spicy; serve it as part of a meze or as an accompaniment to anything grilled in a Mediterranean or Middle Eastern vein.
How do I cook the grapes?
After browning the pita, saute the halved grapes in the same pan with no additional oil for about 30 seconds, until warmed through but not falling apart.
Which spice mix is best?
The author's favorite, if pressed, is the "fresh zaatar" variation: toasted sesame seeds, sumac and fresh thyme leaves.
How do I finish the dish?
Toss with a squeeze of lemon, the spices and the cheese, taste, and finish with a drizzle of excellent olive oil; an orange-scented one is a perfect fit. Serve warm.

summary: A review of Alice Currah's Savory Sweet Life cookbook (the 100 recipes are organized by family occasion and are not all vegetarian), with her recipe for roasted carrots with sage brown butter, reprinted with permission: carrots roasted 20 minutes at 400°F and tossed in cinnamon-nutmeg brown butter.
glance: Savory Sweet Life: 100 Simply Delicious Recipes for Every Family Occasion by Alice
12 carrots roasted at 400°F for 20 minutes, tossed in sage brown butter
3 tablespoons butter, 6 sage leaves, cinnamon and nutmeg, 1 to 2 minutes
Vegetarian, gluten-free and kosher (the book itself is not vegetarian)
faq: Is Savory Sweet Life a vegetarian cookbook?
No. The book is not vegetarian, but there are plenty of vegetarian dishes and many more that can easily be made without meat.
How is the book organized?
Each chapter is an occasion, like Father's Day, Family Game Night or Summer Fun in the Sun, which can jog your imagination when planning an upcoming event, big or small.
What are the recipes like?

Genuine and without pretense: well conceived, straightforward to make and full of flavor. Alice doesn't eschew shortcuts when they make sense but won't compromise taste for a 10-minute meal that isn't worth the 10 minutes.
How do I make the roasted carrots with sage brown butter?

Toss 12 carrots (peeled, halved lengthwise and cut in 2-inch pieces) with olive oil and roast at 400°F about 20 minutes until tender. Meanwhile melt 3 tablespoons of butter with chopped sage, cinnamon and nutmeg until fragrant, brown and beginning to foam, 1 to 2 minutes, then toss the carrots in it.
Can I vary the carrots?
The author left small, sweet carrots whole; cut larger ones as described. You could also add toasted pecans, or sprinkle a little brown sugar on the carrots right before roasting.

summary: Summer squash and portobello vegetarian lasagna: thinly sliced squash and portobello caps thoroughly sauteed and caramelized first, layered with no-boil noodles, lemony tomato sauce, seasoned ricotta and mozzarella and baked at 375°F; prep 30 minutes, cook 1 hour, serves at least 8.
glance: 11 x 13 inches, at least 2 inches deep, about 4 layers
internal temperature about 170°F, rest at least 15 minutes
faq: How do I keep vegetable lasagna from being watery?
Both the squash and portobellos are thoroughly sauteed first, in single layers over high heat on both sides until well browned, to maximize flavor and minimize any watery outbursts.
How do I slice portobellos?
Lay the caps down flat and slice them on the bias, a trick the author learned at Cafe Flora while making hundreds of Wellingtons and French Dips.
Are portobellos still relevant?
The author's brother asked. They're an overused vegetarian cliche because they are thought a stand-in for meat, but properly prepared they have good flavor and texture.
How do I know the lasagna is done?

When the internal temperature is about 170°F or you can easily pierce the noodles with a fork and the sauce is bubbling around the sides. Cover with foil part of the time if it browns too much, and finish under the broiler if the cheese isn't crispy enough.
How do I use no-boil noodles?
Get them quite wet: build layers of noodles, sauce on every layer, squash and mushrooms, ricotta mixture or mozzarella. Regular noodles should be par-boiled.
How long should I let it rest?
At least 15 minutes before serving so it has time to set up.

summary: Baked appetizer cheese empanadas with quick chimichurri: a butter, egg and milk dough rolled into 5-inch circles, filled with grated cheese (about 20% romano) and onion, sealed and baked at 425°F for about 20 minutes; makes 3 dozen two-bite appetizers.
glance: 425°F for about 20 minutes, until deep golden brown
6 cups grated melting cheese, minced onion and cayenne
assemble ahead and refrigerate or freeze, then reheat on baking sheets
faq: What cheese works in empanadas?
Any cheese that melts well. Latin American cheeses are a good choice, and the author included about 20% romano for depth of flavor.
How do I keep the cheese from leaking out?

Wet the edge with a pastry brush, fill each with a heaping tablespoon, fold over and press firmly for a good seal. Any cheese that leaks and makes a crispy brown puddle on the sheet pan is a Cook's Treat.
Can I bake them instead of frying?

Yes, these are baked: brush with a little whole milk for a shine and bake at 425°F for about 20 minutes. You can do everything ahead and refrigerate or freeze, then reheat on baking sheets for a few minutes.
How do I make the dough?

Cut cold butter into flour, baking powder and salt, beat the milk with the eggs and add them, working quickly to form a ball. Divide in 3, refrigerate at least 20 minutes, then roll and cut into twelve 5-inch circles per ball.
How do I make the chimichurri?
A quickie version: whir parsley, onion, garlic, olive oil, lemon juice and oregano in a food processor to a medium-coarse sauce, and let it marry for about half an hour.

summary: Smoked pineapple and tomatillo salsa: pineapple chunks smoked 5 minutes over wood chips in a covered pot, tomatillos and green onions dry-roasted 5 minutes, then pureed with jalapeno, cilantro, salt and agave; the author no longer recommends this stovetop smoking method.
glance: at least 3 days in the refrigerator
tomatillos and green onions in a dry skillet about 5 minutes
at room temperature, on tacos, quesadillas and chilaquiles
faq: Is stovetop smoking safe?

The author's note says he no longer recommends jury-rigged stovetop smoking, having learned that creating smoke in a low-oxygen sealed environment creates unnecessarily high levels of carcinogens. His Smoked Tofu Buns recipe has a safer alternative if you don't have your own smoking method; ensure adequate ventilation and only do it if you know how to do it safely.
How does smoking change a fruit salsa?
Fruit salsas risk being too sweet, but smoking tempers the pineapple's sweetness and the tomatillos are quite tart. The author still added 1 to 2 tablespoons of agave to balance.
How long does the salsa keep?
At least 3 days in the refrigerator; serve at room temperature for best flavor.
What do I eat it with?
The author ate it all week on tacos, quesadillas and chilaquiles.
Can I smoke two things with one batch of chips?
No. If you also make frijoles charros, don't try to get enough smoke from one batch of wood chips: you won't get the best flavor if you run them too long.

summary: Fresh fettuccine with hedgehog mushrooms and ricotta: mushrooms sauteed in butter about 8 minutes, tossed with fresh pasta boiled just a few minutes, and topped with a dollop of fresh ricotta, lemon zest, salt and pepper; a weeknight dinner for 4.
glance: 1 pound fresh fettuccine, cooked just a few minutes
1 pound hedgehog, chanterelle, shiitake or king oyster, sauteed about 8 minutes
1 pound fresh, preferably Calabro, brought out of the fridge first
faq: What are hedgehog mushrooms?

They taste very much like chanterelles but are a little less expensive and have a later season. If they're unavailable, cultivated shiitakes (available year-round) or king oyster mushrooms also work; probably not standard white buttons.
Is fresh or dried pasta better?

Italians say it's not a question of one being better; they're different, and each marries best with a certain range of sauces. Fresh pasta is especially well suited to cream sauces, and a big dollop of fresh ricotta is the world's simplest cream sauce.
Where do I find fresh pasta?

At many farmer's markets or in the refrigerator section of a good grocer; quality varies, so you may have to experiment to find a brand you like. Making it yourself turns a weeknight dinner into a project.
How long does fresh pasta take to cook?
Usually just a few minutes, less than dried. Taste a bite frequently and stop the moment it's done, then toss with a tablespoon of butter.
Why take the ricotta out of the fridge?
So it isn't ice cold when you serve it.

summary: Spanish lentil and mushroom stew: French green lentils simmered about 20 minutes and seasoned with sherry vinegar and smoked paprika, topped with thick-cut, well-browned crimini mushrooms and a cherry tomato and basil salad; vegan, 40 minutes.
glance: 2 cups French green (or de Puy or black Beluga), about 20 minutes
faq: What lentils should I use?
French green lentils (lentils de Puy) or black Beluga lentils. Don't use standard big green or brown lentils because they will turn to mush.
Why cut the mushrooms thick?
Mushrooms cut thickly and browned are a completely different experience from thin sauteed slices: the surface gets seared and the interior stays chewy instead of cooking all the water out.
How do I cook the lentils?

Saute onion and garlic in olive oil about 3 minutes, add the lentils and 4 cups of water, bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer and cook uncovered until tender but not falling apart, about 20 minutes. Drain, then season with smoked paprika, salt and sherry vinegar.
What is the cherry tomato salad for?

Especially with earthy, brown plates of food, the author likes to finish with something bright and fresh for visual interest and lighter flavors: halved cherry tomatoes and basil tossed with olive oil, sherry vinegar and salt.
What do I serve it with?
A good baguette makes it a nice light meal for four, or smaller portions can be the first course of a more elaborate meal for six.

summary: Saffron risotto with watercress puree and spring vegetables: arborio rice cooked with white wine and saffron-infused broth added a cup at a time and finished with lemon zest and taleggio, served over a watercress puree with sauteed peas and asparagus; 1 hour, 6 servings.
glance: Prep 30 min, cook 30 min, total 1 hr
2 cups arborio (420 grams) with 1 1/4 cups white wine and 6 cups simmering broth
1/4 pound taleggio and lemon zest, texture all'onda (wavy)
faq: Do you have to stir risotto continuously?
No. The author says don't believe the hype: it's entirely adequate to stir it frequently, and you'll get a perfectly creamy result.
How do I know when risotto is done?
Cook it until the rice is quite tender but not completely falling apart into rice pudding; there should be a hint of resistance when you bite a grain.
How loose should risotto be?

Finish it with plenty of cheese and enough broth that it is almost pourable: all'onda (wavy), not so thick it stands up by itself. It should be quite moist or it will firm up too much when plated; use simmering water if you run out of broth.
How do I add the saffron?
Wrap it in tin foil and toast briefly in a dry skillet, then cool, crumble and add it to the simmering vegetable broth.
Can I change the vegetables?
Yes. The author might do the puree with nettles instead of watercress and top it with fava beans and hedgehog mushrooms rather than English peas and asparagus, depending on what's fresh.
How do I add the broth?
After the wine is absorbed, ladle in about 1 cup of broth, stir well, and repeat every couple of minutes as the liquid is absorbed, tasting a grain periodically.

summary: Pan-roasted tomatillo salsa verde: 1.5 pounds of tomatillos, 8 cloves of garlic and 3 to 6 serrano chiles roasted in a dry pan about 4 minutes per side, then blended with onion, salt and olive oil and strained; yields about 2.5 cups.
glance: dry pan, about 4 minutes per side, until the tomatillos are quite soft
faq: What are tomatillos?
Green tomato-like fruit wrapped in a papery husk, usually found in the specialty produce part of a grocery. Buy 8 or 10, around 1.5 pounds.
Is salsa verde hard to make at home?
No, it's ridiculously easy and tastes way better than the jarred version. Pan-roast the tomatillos, garlic and chiles, then blend with onion, salt and olive oil and strain.
What are other ways to cook the tomatillos?
You can boil them whole, or oven roast them, and you can optionally fry the finished sauce in some oil to deepen and intensify the flavors.
How do I change the flavor?
Add cilantro, epazote or oregano; add chipotles for smoky spice; or use more serranos or jalapenos for more heat. This version is pretty garlicky with medium heat.
What can I do with salsa verde?
Serve it at the table with any Mexican dish, as a dip for tortillas, fry eggs in it, or use it as a sauce for enchiladas verde.

summary: Kasha pilaf with dates, pistachios and baharat: buckwheat groats coated in egg and dried in the pan about 4 minutes, simmered covered about 12 minutes in butter and water, then fluffed with baharat, black pepper, diced dates and toasted pistachios; serves 4 as a side.
glance: about 4 minutes to dry the egg-coated kasha, then about 12 minutes covered
faq: What is kasha?

Simply whole grain buckwheat kernels, a staple food in Eastern Europe with a nutty, almost haunting flavor. It is often found in the Jewish foods section of a grocery store; Wolff's is a common brand, and medium or whole granulation is best.
Is kasha gluten-free?
Yes. Buckwheat kasha is gluten-free; despite the name it is unrelated to wheat.
Why coat the kasha with egg?
Stir the egg into the kasha until the grains are coated and cook, stirring pretty constantly, about 4 minutes until the grains dry out and separate, so the pilaf stays fluffy rather than mushy.
What is baharat?
A wonderful Middle Eastern spice blend with tremendous complexity: sweet, hot, floral and mouthwatering. You can make your own, or try dukkah or ras el hanout.
Why add the pistachios at the end?
Toast them lightly in a dry skillet and mix them in just before serving; if you do it much in advance they absorb moisture and lose their crunch.
Can I use other grains?
The author thinks couscous or freekeh would also work, though he hasn't tried.
